description: Ed25519 to X25519 conversion during key-agreement recipient selection. Both key literals come from the W3C-CCG did:key method specification's Ed25519/X25519 worked example: the Ed25519 signing key z6Mkha... and the X25519 key-agreement key z6LSj7... the spec derives from it. The expected X25519 value is the spec's own published counterpart, independently decoded from its publicKeyMultibase — it is NOT produced by the Rust conversion on the expected side, so this is a genuine conformance check of the birational Edwards-to-Montgomery map rather than a tautology.

vector.note: The document below is constructed for this assertion — did:key itself publishes no keyAgreement relationship, and the resolver deliberately keeps did:key signing-only. Only the key literals are taken from the spec; they are what the assertion checks.

cases.description: keyAgreement names an Ed25519 verification method. Upstream converts such a key to X25519 rather than rejecting it (packages/agent/src/dwn-encryption.ts), so selection returns the Montgomery form of the Ed25519 point while preserving the source verification-method id unchanged.

verification.tool: pure-Python base58btc decoder + multicodec strip + base64url, plus the birational map u = (1+y)/(1-y) mod 2^255-19 computed directly from the Ed25519 point — neither via the Rust impl
verification.note: The X25519 hex derived by the birational map equals the hex decoded from the spec's published x25519Multibase, so the two independent derivations agree before the impl is consulted.
